@carlory Is `feature.CPUManager` related to the Kubelet feature `CPUManager`? If so, should we also remove it from e2e configs and tests?

@bart0sh, these tests need NUMA support available on the given node. We can not assume that every node has NUMA support. i.e.,

```
$ (base) ➜  test-infra git:(master) docker exec -it demo-control-plane bash
root@demo-control-plane:/# numactl -s
physcpubind: 0 1 2 3 4 5 6 7
No NUMA support available on this system.
root@demo-control-plane:/#
```

I added a comment to the feature label in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/129296/commits/61a4fe2f141ab6ba54dbd6c327f953c7310abfae. 

FYI: 
- https://github.com/kubernetes/test-infra/pull/30545
- https://github.com/kubernetes/test-infra/blob/6ea573b75e0746a382c26f7ed86325ac41e21e6b/config/jobs/kubernetes/sig-node/node-kubelet.yaml#L187

@carlory
> these tests need NUMA support 

So, I assume that answer to my question `Is feature.CPUManager related to the Kubelet feature CPUManager?` is `No`, right? It's used to signal that the test has to be run on a node with NUMA support. Should we, then rename the feature gate used in tests to something like 'RequiresNUMA' and stop using removed feature gates to avoid confusion?

I'm not saying we should do this in this PR. Creating an issue should be enough at this point.
@bart0sh created an issue.

/lgtm

for approval

> @carlory Is `feature.CPUManager` related to the Kubelet feature `CPUManager`? If so, should we also remove it from e2e configs and tests?

I'm not the person being asked but still: yes it used to.
I think we still very much want a label for e2e test which is applied to all the tests pertaining to `cpumanager`, so we can run just these tests.

Or, to put differently: if we use just one label for all the tests (!!), how can I just run the `cpumanager` tests? why should not that be supported?

> @bart0sh, these tests need NUMA support available on the given node. We can not assume that every node has NUMA support. i.e.,


Hey, thanks for your work in this issue! most of cpumanager proper tests don't require multiple NUMA nodes, but they will require multiple (like 8 or so) cores available. All the tests I'm aware of try to detect the machine capabilities and skip if their requirement are not met.

Yes, this is unfortunate and weaken our signal, but unless (if ever) we fix the CI machine configuration moving to more expensive configs, not much we can do.

> how can I just run the cpumanager tests? why should not that be supported?

If so, we need to keep the feature label CPUManager and close https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/130579. I have no opinion on this.

>  we need to keep the feature label CPUManager and close #130579. I have no opinion on this.

Agreed, please close, thanks!

issue_context.title: Clean up featue labels for resource managers
issue_context.body:
1. Introduce a new feature label named `RequiresNUMA` to replace `CPUManager`, `MemoryManager` and `TopologyManager`.
2. Introduce a new job like `ci-kubernetes-node-kubelet-serial-resource-managers` to replace `ci-kubernetes-node-kubelet-serial-topology-manager`, `ci-kubernetes-node-kubelet-serial-cpu-manager` and `ci-kubernetes-node-kubelet-serial-memory-manager`.

Related to https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/129296#issuecomment-2700038459

Thanks for filing this issue! cleanup in this area is surely welcome. Few questions for my understanding
  
> 1. Introduce a new feature label named `RequiresNUMA` to replace `CPUManager`, `MemoryManager` and `TopologyManager`.

This seems like a good idea, but why replace and not just adding?

>      2. Introduce a new job like `ci-kubernetes-node-kubelet-serial-resource-managers` to replace `ci-kubernetes-node-kubelet-serial-topology-manager`, `ci-kubernetes-node-kubelet-serial-cpu-manager` and `ci-kubernetes-node-kubelet-serial-memory-manager`.

Some tests are already pretty slow, wha'ts the advantage in consolidating them?
